topics.observableQuestion: What changes when a germ cell makes gametes: sets, copies, shape or signals?

topics.priorKnowledgeSupport: A chromosome carries DNA. A set contains one of each chromosome type; replication makes sister copies without adding homologous sets. Hormones act through suitable target responses.

retrieval.prompt: After meiosis I in the human model, give sets, chromosomes and DNA molecules per cell.
retrieval.comparisonGuide: One set, 23 duplicated chromosomes and 46 DNA molecules per cell.

evidenceSlip.prompt: Explain how a fall in testosterone could be followed by a rise in LH in the intact feedback model, including one condition.

frames.title: Gametes and chromosome sets
frames.scenario: A primary spermatocyte has completed DNA replication. Count human chromosome sets, chromosomes and DNA molecules before meiosis I and in one product after meiosis I.
orderedExplanation: Begin with two homologous sets and 46 chromosomes.
Replication creates two chromatids per chromosome: 92 DNA molecules, still two sets.
Meiosis I separates homologues: each product has one set, 23 chromosomes and 46 DNA molecules.
frames.conclusion: Before meiosis I: 2 sets, 46 chromosomes, 92 DNA molecules. After meiosis I, per cell: 1 set, 23 chromosomes, 46 DNA molecules.

frames.title: Division and differentiation
frames.scenario: One typical primary spermatocyte completes both meiotic divisions. Predict the immediate products and explain why they still need further change.
orderedExplanation: Meiosis I produces two secondary spermatocytes with duplicated chromosomes.
Meiosis II separates sister chromatids, producing four haploid spermatids.
Differentiation reshapes each spermatid, including its acrosome, compact nucleus and flagellum.
frames.conclusion: The immediate products are four haploid spermatids. Meiosis establishes their chromosome content; differentiation and later maturation support the form and functions associated with sperm.
frames.status: narration-bound; reviewed illustration and rendered sequencing pending

frames.title: Hormone sources and targets
frames.scenario: In a simplified pathway, GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary, which releases LH. Identify the next target and response, then contrast the FSH branch.

Trace LH to interstitial cells and testosterone release.
Trace FSH to Sertoli-cell support within seminiferous tubules; connect this branch with local testosterone action.
frames.conclusion: LH acts on interstitial cells to support testosterone production. FSH acts through Sertoli cells to support germ-cell development. The branches interact but do not have identical targets.

retrieval.prompt: Distinguish a follicle, an oocyte and a corpus luteum.
retrieval.comparisonGuide: A follicle surrounds an oocyte; remaining follicular tissue forms the corpus luteum after ovulation.

frames.title: Ovaries and supporting tissues
frames.scenario: An ovarian diagram shows a large follicle containing an oocyte and, elsewhere, a corpus luteum. A student labels both structures “eggs.” Correct the diagram.

Label the follicle as a supporting structure containing the oocyte.
Label the corpus luteum as tissue formed from the follicle after ovulation, with a hormone-secreting role.

frames.title: Oogenesis and meiotic pauses
frames.scenario: Compare a typical human primary oocyte before completion of meiosis I with the secondary oocyte released at ovulation. State the pause and chromosome-copy condition.

The secondary oocyte is haploid with duplicated chromosomes and is typically paused in metaphase II at ovulation.

topics.priorKnowledgeSupport: Hormone sources and targets form pathways. Negative feedback opposes a change; positive feedback can reinforce it within defined conditions. Graph axes identify time and the measured quantity.

retrieval.prompt: Distinguish ovulation from menstruation and name one associated hormone change.
retrieval.comparisonGuide: Ovulation releases an oocyte after an LH surge; menstruation sheds endometrium as luteal hormone support declines.

evidenceSlip.prompt: Use one sampled hormone pattern to connect an ovarian event with an endometrial response, keeping a timing or scale limit explicit.

frames.title: Two coordinated cycles
frames.scenario: Place follicle development, ovulation, corpus-luteum function, endometrial rebuilding and secretory maintenance on two aligned tracks in a typical simplified cycle.
orderedExplanation: Use an ovarian track for follicular phase → ovulation → luteal phase.
Use a uterine track for shedding → rebuilding → secretory maintenance.
Align the tracks by changing hormone signals, rather than calling a uterine event an ovarian structure.

frames.title: Follicle growth and changing feedback
frames.scenario: In the supplied series, estrogen's relative index rises to 10 on day 12 and LH peaks at 18 on day 14. Explain a plausible connection and one limitation of these data.
orderedExplanation: Find day 12 on the time axis. Read the estrogen index as 10 on its own relative scale.
Find day 14 and read the LH peak as 18 on the LH scale. The LH peak comes after the estrogen rise. Do not compare 18 with 10 as if they were amounts on a shared concentration scale.
Connect the order to the mechanism: sustained high estrogen near ovulation can increase upstream activity through positive feedback, helping produce an LH surge.
State the limit: the sample points are two days apart, and other conditions were not measured. The pattern supports the connection but does not prove an exact trigger level or hour of ovulation.
frames.conclusion: The pattern is consistent with an estrogen-associated feedback transition preceding an LH surge. The sampled indices do not by themselves prove a universal threshold or the exact hour of ovulation.

frames.title: Corpus luteum and the endometrium
frames.scenario: In a cycle without an ongoing pregnancy signal, corpus-luteum function declines. Predict the effect on progesterone support and the endometrium.

Follow reduced luteal function to declining hormone support.
Connect withdrawal of support with endometrial breakdown and shedding in the model.

frames.title: Graphs and cycle variation

Identify day 21 as the highest sampled value, while leaving the intervals between samples uncertain.

topics.priorKnowledgeSupport: Gametes contain one chromosome set. The uterine tube and endometrium are different locations. Cell number, total size and developmental organization describe different changes.

retrieval.prompt: Put fertilization, cleavage, blastocyst formation and implantation in order.
retrieval.comparisonGuide: Fertilization → cleavage → blastocyst formation → implantation in a suitable endometrium.

evidenceSlip.prompt: Locate one IVF step in the developmental sequence and explain an outcome it supports without guaranteeing the next step.

frames.title: Gametes meet
frames.scenario: An oocyte and sperm are present in a fictional uterine-tube model, but the sperm cannot complete the interactions needed to pass the oocyte's coverings and fuse with its membrane. Has fertilization been demonstrated?
orderedExplanation: Distinguish shared location from successful cellular interaction.
Identify passage through surrounding coverings and membrane fusion as necessary events in the model.
Seek evidence of activation and combining parental genetic contributions before calling the sequence complete.
frames.conclusion: No. The presence of both gametes in the same region is insufficient. The failed interaction interrupts the sequence before the full fertilization process is established.

frames.title: Combining chromosome sets
frames.scenario: A normal human sperm contributes 23 chromosomes and the female gamete contributes 23. A hypothetical error allows a second complete sperm contribution. Compare the set totals without predicting an individual outcome.
orderedExplanation: One paternal set plus one maternal set restores two sets: 46 chromosomes.
A second paternal set would add another 23 in this simplified counting model.
Distinguish the resulting three-set count from a normal diploid fertilization.
frames.conclusion: The normal combination is 2n = 46. The hypothetical additional complete contribution gives three sets, 69 chromosomes, showing why mechanisms restricting extra sperm entry matter.

frames.title: Cleavage and blastocyst formation
frames.scenario: A simplified embryo changes from one cell to two, four and eight while its overall outer size remains similar. What changed, and what did not follow from the observation?

Recognize cleavage as repeated divisions distributing the original material into smaller cells.
Separate increased cell number from an increase in the embryo's total external size.

frames.title: Gastrulation establishes layers

Use coordinated cell movement and three-layer organization to identify gastrulation.
